name: redpanda-docs skill vs docs
description: Measures whether the redpanda-docs skill changes how an agent uses the Redpanda Docs MCP tools: looking up properties for the version the user's cluster runs, and what to do when the anonymous allowance runs out. The docs tools are mocked in every arm, so the cases grade the agent's use of them, not the published docs.

test_cases.query: A teammate says they changed min_cleanable_dirty_ratio on our self-managed Redpanda cluster a while back. Is it still at its default value? If it isn't, give me the command to put it back to the default, but don't run it. You can run rpk on the admin host with run_rpk, and the Redpanda docs tools are available.
test_cases.why: The docs tools answer for the latest release unless given a version, and an rpk client's own version is not the cluster's. Here rpk is a 26.2 client, the brokers run 25.3, and the cluster's value is 0.5. The default of min_cleanable_dirty_ratio is 0.2 in v25.3.11 and v26.1.14 and 0.5 in v26.2.4 (the published property datasets, which the mocked docs tools answer from), so an agent that looks the default up for the latest release tells the user the value is unchanged. The redpanda-docs skill says to establish the cluster's version (rpk version under Redpanda Cluster, or the brokers list) and pass it to the lookup. rpk shows no defaults, so the cluster cannot give the answer away.

mock.name: get_config_property
mock.description: Look up one Redpanda configuration property (cluster, broker, or topic) by exact name and return its documented type, default, description, restart and enterprise flags, Redpanda Cloud availability, related properties, and docs URL. Deterministic: it reads the generated property dataset for the requested docs version, so a property that does not exist returns found=false with close-name suggestions instead of a guess, and no LLM or search is involved. Use this before ask_redpanda_question for any question about a specific property's default, type, or availability. Pass platform='cloud' to learn whether the property is supported or editable in Redpanda Cloud.

name.description: Exact property name, e.g. 'log_segment_size' or 'cleanup.policy'. Aliases are accepted.

version.description: Docs version as its URL spells it ('26.1'), 'current' for the latest release, or a release tag ('v26.2.4'). Omit for the latest release. An unknown value returns found=false with the list of published versions. Ignored when platform is 'cloud', which always answers from the latest release.

platform.description: 'cloud' answers for Redpanda Cloud (Cloud availability, the Cloud docs page); 'self-managed' (the default) answers for Self-Managed Redpanda.

context.description: Optional. In one concise sentence (third person), describe what the user is trying to accomplish with this request. Do not include credentials, tokens, personal data, or verbatim secrets.

session_goal.description: Optional. In one concise sentence (third person), the overall goal of this session: what the user is trying to get done, not just this call. Send the same goal on every call in the session, and update it only if the goal changes. Do not include credentials, tokens, personal data, or verbatim secrets.

mock.name: ask_redpanda_question
mock.description: Search the official Redpanda documentation and return the most relevant sections from it for a user query. Each returned section includes the url and its actual content in markdown. Use this tool for all queries that require Redpanda knowledge. Results are ordered by relevance, with the most relevant result returned first. If you know the user's deployment platform, pass "platform" so results from the other platform's docs are excluded. Note that "platform" filters the sections already retrieved rather than re-running the search, so it can return substantially fewer sections: on a broker-level question where most matches come from the other platform's docs, it can cut a 15-section response to 1 or 2. Omit "platform" if you would rather have more context and judge platform relevance yourself from each section's url. If you know which Redpanda version the user runs, pass "version" (use 'current' for the latest release; its release number is also accepted). Unlike "platform", "version" is applied during retrieval, so it does not shrink the result set: it stops the same page being returned once per indexed version, which is otherwise most of the response. Version-neutral docs (Cloud, Connect, Agentic Data Plane, API reference) are always included. Omitting "version" searches the latest release.

question.description: The question to search the docs for. Required.

query.description: Alias for "question", for clients that use that name. Prefer "question".

platform.description: The user's deployment platform. 'cloud' excludes Self-Managed sections; 'self-managed' excludes Redpanda Cloud sections. Platform-neutral docs (Connect, API reference, labs) are always kept. Applied after retrieval, so it shrinks the result set rather than finding more of the right platform's pages. Omit to search all docs.

version.description: Docs version to search, written as the docs URLs spell it (23.3, 24.1, 24.2, 24.3, 25.1, 25.2, 25.3, 26.1, current). Use 'current' for the latest release; a release number newer than every listed one is also read as the latest release. Applied at retrieval, so unlike "platform" it does not shrink the result set: every section returned is from this version, plus version-neutral docs (Cloud, Connect, Agentic Data Plane, API reference), which are always included. Omit to search the latest release. Any other value is rejected with the list of valid versions.

top_k.description: Maximum number of sections to return, applied after platform filtering. Must be a positive integer.

context.description: Optional. In one concise sentence (third person), describe what the user is trying to accomplish with this request. Do not include credentials, tokens, personal data, or verbatim secrets.

session_goal.description: Optional. In one concise sentence (third person), the overall goal of this session: what the user is trying to get done, not just this call. Send the same goal on every call in the session, and update it only if the goal changes. Do not include credentials, tokens, personal data, or verbatim secrets.

invariants.name: default_for_cluster_version
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer says the cluster's min_cleanable_dirty_ratio of 0.5 is the default or unchanged, or gives a revert command that sets it to 0.5. Passes if it identifies the brokers' version as 25.3, says the default in that release is 0.2 so the value was changed, and gives a command that sets it back to 0.2 (for example rpk cluster config set min_cleanable_dirty_ratio 0.2), even if it also notes that the default is 0.5 in later releases.

test_cases.query: Using the Redpanda docs tools, what's the default value of the cluster property log_compaction_interval_ms on self-managed Redpanda 26.1, and does changing it need a restart?
test_cases.why: When the anonymous Docs MCP allowance runs out, every docs tool call returns a quota refusal. With no way to fetch the Markdown pages, the redpanda-docs skill says to tell the user to run /mcp and sign in with a Redpanda Cloud account, and not to answer from memory. A model without the skill relays the refusal's generic reconnect advice, or answers from memory as if it had looked the value up.

invariants.name: no_unverified_answer
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer states a default value or restart requirement for log_compaction_interval_ms as fact, without saying it could not check it in the docs, or does not tell the user how to lift the limit by signing in. Passes if it says the docs lookup was refused for quota, tells the user to run /mcp and sign in with a Redpanda Cloud account (or sign in at docs.redpanda.com/login and reconnect through /mcp), and either gives no value or clearly marks any value it gives as unverified from memory, optionally pointing at the property's docs page.
